title: Perspective
paragraphs: Thanks to the airship we seized from Takt, we enjoyed a leisurely journey through the sky. Of course, since only one person was needed to register a portal at each destination, we split up and acted separately. The travel itself was easy, so by nightfall, we would dock and return to the castle to rest.
By the way, you can’t save a portal’s location while inside the airship, so it has to be docked. It would be more convenient if we could move freely while the airship was traveling.
“Hm, I was thinking…” Ren spoke while eating dinner that night.

Since Ren and Itsuki insisted, Father gave instructions in the kitchen and oversaw the preparation of the meal. A variety of dishes were laid out. Of course, a little further away, the royal family living in the castle was also dining, so the hall itself was fairly large. The royals were paying attention to us, but thanks to the Pig King’s advice, they seemed hesitant to speak. It’s risky to get too close to the heroes in Faubrey. Father and the others had been subtly refusing any offers. Many of the dishes were similar to what we had eaten in Japan. Currently, the castle’s cooks in Faubrey are desperately learning how to cook from Father, as Éclair had reported. It seems their job is to prepare food that suits the taste of the heroes.
“What is it?”
“They said back in Melromarc that the heroes’ weapons repel each other and cause problems when we act together, but in reality, I don’t feel any issues.”
“That’s true. To be honest, I don’t really see the need for us to act separately.”
“Yeah, I guess. Maybe it’s only a bit inconvenient when leveling up?”
“If necessary, whether it’s Motoyasu or Father, they can just borrow each other’s allies and manage somehow.”
Ren’s view is completely different from that of the previous loop. That being said, there’s no disagreement with what he’s saying. The Filolials love running, and they enjoy hunting as well.
“Borrowing allies… Yeah, that’s right. There’s no need for them to be exclusive companions. Even the heroes can cooperate.”
“Based on Motoyasu’s story, just being able to think this way is already progress, isn’t it?”
“Is that so?”
“Motoyasu said that Ren had issues with teamwork and struggled with coordination. Remember the problem we had when we hunted together before?”
“Ah, yeah. That happened. It was when Itsuki pointed it out. It wasn’t that long ago, but it feels a bit nostalgic.”
“Yes, it was about how Ren was scary because he almost hit me, right?”
That did happen. I remember it as well. Father had mentioned that Ren would be better off taking a step back and observing his surroundings while fighting.
“I think Ren can now move in a way that doesn’t cause problems when acting with us. Of course, everyone else has probably also gotten better at adjusting to Ren’s movements.”
Ren tilted his head at Father’s analysis.
“Motoyasu said that Ren and Wyndia would argue so much that their coordination was a complete mess.”
“Is that true?”
“Is it?”
Assistant asked Ren about it along with Rival.

“It’s a story from a different time than now. In that world, Ren unknowingly killed Wyndia’s father, and he ended up provoking Wyndia’s wrath when she was trying to sever that grudge and fight for the sake of the world.”
“Hmm…”
Well, the current Assistant probably thinks it’s irrelevant. In fact, compared to the previous Assistant, this one lacks a certain seriousness… or something.
“The coordination was a mess. They almost hit each other while attacking, and sometimes they were about to get hit by the enemy’s attacks.”
“Naofumi, that story is…”
Ren looked a little embarrassed. Well, what follows after that is a pretty harsh story.
“Hmm… But now, when I fight alongside the Sword Hero, I don’t feel anything off.”
“That’s probably the difference between the previous loop and this one. Ren grew stronger by fighting together with everyone.”
“Is that how it works? I thought it was supposed to be something more difficult…”
“Even during the battle in Melromarc, you were mindful of Imiya, weren’t you? Motoyasu also noticed that point.”

When Father pointed this out, Ren muttered “Ah,” as if he realized it. Now that he mentions it, that’s true. The Ren from the previous world wouldn’t have paid any attention to the rear guard during battle.
“The old Ren would have completely excluded Imiya from his thoughts. And if she got in the way, he’d probably say something like, ‘Stop wandering around!’”
At that, Ren made a slightly complicated expression. Itsuki whispered into my ear.
“He probably remembers something. He must have done that while playing games back then.”
“Indeed.”
Ren glared at us. Did we hit the mark?
“Well, well. But how about now? You can fight even when Imiya is nearby, right?”
“Now that you mention it… yeah.”
“Feels like your perspective has broadened.”
Ren didn’t seem entirely displeased.
“Still… I don’t know. I thought there’d be a more obvious moment where I could tell I’d gotten stronger.”

Ren answered quietly. Indeed, realizing you’ve gotten stronger is something that happens without noticing. After all, I remember the days when I was chasing pigs’ backs while training with a weapon. I did a bit of practice when I was getting along with a pig who was into kendo as a hobby.
“Getting stronger is usually like that. Well, in a world where there are levels and clear methods for strengthening, it’s harder to notice.”
Father dished up some food onto a plate and handed it to Ren. Truly, just an extension of everyday life.
“In time, you find yourself able to do things you couldn’t before. It’s the same with online games, isn’t it?”
“Yeah… I’ve had similar experiences in VR games.”
“I feel like Ren’s experiences lean more toward PvP games. You probably didn’t play much, but if it were a genre like FPS, you might have picked it up… maybe.”
“Knowing Ren, he probably charged recklessly and got shot down! Then he must have called it a trash game and quit!”
“What was that!?”
Ren stood up, shouting. I recognize that reaction.
“Come on now, Motoyasu, why are you provoking him…”
“FPS, huh.”
“Itsuki, have you played it?”
“In the game world, individuals with certain abilities are often restricted. Even if they can play, they’re matched only against others with similar abilities.”
“Ah…”

Since Itsuki has the ability of accuracy, if he were to play a shooting game, he would likely crush ordinary players. However, if he could only fight against others with similar abilities, winning would be difficult. I wouldn’t want to play a game that leaves me feeling that miserable. Come to think of it, it seems these supernatural abilities apply even in games.
“Well, in FPS games and such, there’s often that feeling of getting stronger without realizing it. Ren, you’ve had moments where you felt your swordsmanship improved, right?”

According to Father, FPS games are the kind where one shot often results in instant death. Experiencing those kinds of gunfights and accumulating experience gives you a sense of getting stronger. Learning techniques to take down opponents without getting killed… it’s apparently a great way to develop teamwork and situational awareness in team battles.
“Is that how it is?”
“Yeah, that’s usually how it works.”
Father had certainly noticed Ren’s growth.
“That said… I’m still trying to figure out how to refine my skills.”
“True… mastering martial arts using a shield is quite difficult.”
“Grappling moves are off-limits, so all I can really do is grab and pin down my opponent.”
“There are weapons like that in fighting games, but shields are treated more like weapons in that case.”
“Normally, you could probably use a shield like a blunt weapon, but status-wise, that’s difficult.”
“From what I’ve heard from Motoyasu about my past self, I understand the theory about deflecting impact, but in practice, it’s just about using skills.”
Father is also trying to move forward day by day.
“Phew, I’m full!”
Sakura-chan and the other Filolials rubbed their bellies contentedly.
“Shall we wrap up the meal soon?”
“But… I haven’t eaten much yet…”
Since Father was cooking, he was behind everyone else.
“Still, hanging around here drinking and fooling around doesn’t seem right.”
“Besides, Ren and Itsuki are underage, aren’t they?”
“It’s another world, so it should be fine.”
“It’s not fine. If you get too deep into that stuff, you’ll end up like the king of Faubrey…”
Father is strict. Although, in the previous loops, Ren and Itsuki drank quite a bit.
“Well, in any case, we have time until Naofumi finishes eating.”
“I’ll hurry up, so just wait a bit.”
“No worries, we’re not in a rush. Maybe I’ll put on a little performance for the first time in a while.”

Itsuki approached the musicians performing in the dining hall and borrowed an instrument. This world has all kinds of instruments. There are instruments like pianos, violins, and many more. I’ve heard that there’s even a musical instrument made from the vocal cords of a monster called a bone throat flute. Among them, Itsuki picked up a violin-like instrument and began to play.
